A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Tensor Decomposition Networks work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, Appendices A–D, and checklists are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original TDN benchmark results, computational measurements, component ablations, and an appendix n-body rank sweep.

after.justification: v4 retains original TDN benchmark results, computational measurements, component ablations, and the appendix n-body rank sweep.

M1.justification: The CP approximation, path-weight sharing, Equiformer-based architecture, and selected rank schedule remain unchanged. v4 discloses that decomposition factors are precomputed and frozen; the PDFs do not establish a change to their training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate PubChemQCR and PubChemQCR-S, OC20 and OC22 IS2RE-DIRECT, and the Appendix D n-body task. The description changes from molecular-dynamics to molecular relaxation snapshots without changing the represented dataset.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the benchmark and ablation comparisons, including EquiformerV2 on OC20, coGN on OC22, and NequIP in the component ablation. Added citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The component ablation's stated energy metric changes from eV in v2 Table 5 to meV/atom in v4 Table 9, introducing per-atom normalization in the label. This is a reported metric revision; recomputation is not established. Splits, training budgets, and retained experimental configurations otherwise match.

E4.justification: The rank-schedule analysis, n-body rank sweep, throughput/component ablations, and TDN/NequIP accuracy ablation are retained. Moving accuracy results to Appendix D and reversing the order of the rank and throughput tables do not add or remove analyses.

E5.justification: Both average equivariance error over 1,000 random rotations and vectors. Neither adds repeated-training-run counts, seed-based uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the checklist's statistical-significance response is identical.

E6.justification: Benchmark scores and matched rank/throughput results remain unchanged. Section 4.1 withdraws the claim that R=7L² achieves the lowest errors, describing an accuracy-efficiency trade-off instead. The ablation narrative also corrects which configuration reduces training time: enabling the components, consistent with 19.0 versus 4.2 minutes per epoch. The energy relabeling does not establish a performance gain.

T1.justification: Theorems 3.1/B.1 replace ceil(R^(1/3)) with floor(R^(1/3)) and add the missing Tucker-truncation-to-CP derivation. Theorems 3.2/B.2 replace the rank-one equivariant-basis argument with a CG-map expansion and explicit coordinate construction at R=d1d2, correcting factor dimensions and establishing a finite rank bound. These substantially revise the central proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and summary retain the same contributions: approximate equivariance through CP decomposition, universality, path-weight sharing, O(L6)-to-O(L4) computation, and competitive accuracy with speedups. Replacing 'single path' with 'single shared parameter set' clarifies the existing mechanism.

C2.justification: v4 explicitly limits the accuracy ablation to relative trends from abbreviated training and distinguishes it from the tuned Table 1 results. It also describes CP savings as storage/space complexity and interprets rank selection through an accuracy-efficiency trade-off. The principal Section 5 limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v4 adds one-time CP precomputation, caching and frozen-factor details, selection by lowest validation energy error, and disclosure that baseline force predictions use gradients except for Equiformer. Existing hardware, training budgets, and AIRS code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds references on canonicalization generalization bounds, smooth and expressive interatomic potentials, and tensor-product expressivity/runtime trade-offs. These modestly extend the discussion of existing research directions without substantially changing the paper's positioning.

P1.justification: Targeted grammar and terminology corrections accompany a refocused efficiency discussion in Section 4.6. Accuracy-ablation discussion moves to Appendix D, whose analyses are reordered. The overall section structure and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Main-text Table 5 becomes a compact training-time table, while its full accuracy comparison appears as Appendix Table 9. The rank and throughput tables exchange order and numbering, and other tables relocate with text reflow. Figures 1–3 retain their graphics and plotted content.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially improves support for two headline theoretical guarantees: Appendix B.2 replaces the unsupported rank-one equivariant-basis construction, and B.1 supplies the missing Tucker-to-CP argument with a corrected rank cutoff. These repair important deficiencies while preserving the empirical evidence. Implementation disclosures and the qualification of ablation conclusions further improve clarity, although the ablation energy relabeling remains unexplained and uncertainty reporting is unchanged.
